sense.text:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.” Look at what is going on in South Africa. They call it xenophobia, prejudice against immigrants: they are telling the black people that look just like them, the Nigerians, the people from Mali, from Ghana, from Ethiopia, that they want them out of their country They are looting their stores, stealing their goods and beating them. It is not xenophobia. It is afrophobia: racism, prejudice and discrimination against black people, by black people. It is self-hatred. It is black-on-black crime.

A Nigerian comes to South Africa, opens a little store, does better than you, and you get upset. It is the same thing you see in the black community in America, where we rob each other, kill each other and hate each other. That is hating thy brother in thine heart.

And Esau is behind it. If you assault somebody you are supposed to go to jail, so where are the police, where are the politicians? Nobody does anything because it is a setup; they want it to happen. A white boy leads Zulu chants and they love him; Europeans get a warm welcome and the crowd dances for them. Nobody tells the white man to get out of South Africa. Only the brothers who came over there to make a living with their little stores and shops.

The ones doing it are the Zulu tribe, and the Zulu tribe is Israel: they are Simeon. Not everybody in South Africa is our people, and it does not mean all of them get in the kingdom, but the Zulu are our people whether you believe it or not.

“Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people.” We as a people have been destroyed in slavery and colonized. We have been taught to hate ourselves and to bear grudges against each other, and it manifests itself through violence: the gun violence in the streets of America, us killing each other. It is no different from what the South Africans are doing.

precepts.why:
“For my people is foolish, they have not known me.” God himself says his people are foolish and have not known him. “They are sottish children”: sottish means stupid. God says his people are stupid children, “and they have none understanding.” He ain’t lying.

Approximately 40 to 50 percent of all the gold ever mined in history came out of South Africa, out of the Witwatersrand basin, the richest gold deposit on earth. The gold rush there began in 1886, and it is what built Johannesburg. That is where all the white people came from and why South Africa was so important to them. That is why apartheid lasted until the ’90s instead of ending in the ’60s, and why the United Nations, formed in the 1940s, never intervened while the people were oppressed: money was being made. Britain was getting the gold out, and they are still extracting it from that same place today.

So where is that gold, and why are the South Africans not rich? Not one of them has that wealth. The white man got all that gold, and he controls 80 percent of the land. Yet a brother over there with a little cart selling shoes and handbags is the one they say is oppressing them, taking South African jobs and resources. They cannot identify who the enemy is: not the Nigerians, not the Ghanaians, not the Ethiopians, but the white man, the one that colonized them and robbed them.

That is why God calls them stupid children with no understanding. It is no different from what Negroes in America are dealing with: you hate yourself, you hate your people, and you cannot tell who the enemy is. You South Africans of the tribe of Simeon are stupid as hell.

“Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.” Ephraim is a silly dove with no heart. “When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.”

That is them South Africans out there marching against the Nigerians and the Ghanaians, which are their brothers, saying they are taking their jobs. Not all of them, but those that are doing it are confused. They are a silly dove.

“Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not.” This is spoken of Ephraim, but the curse that fell upon Ephraim fell upon all the tribes, even the tribes that are in Africa today.

The strength is the riches. Half of all the gold ever mined on this earth came from South Africa, and none of them has any of it: Britain got the gold, the white man got the gold. Strangers devoured their strength and they know it not. Instead they argue with their brothers about their jobs and resources. That is misplaced anger.

“Yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not.” They have grown old under it and still do not understand that strangers are robbing and stealing from them. “And the pride of Israel testifieth to his face: and they do not return to the Lord their God.” They need to be mad at the right people.

sense.text:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be.” The thing that hath been is man. “And that which is done is that which shall be done”: the same thing man did in the past, he is going to come back and do again. “There is no new thing under the sun.” If you were wicked in the past, you are going to be wicked again when you come back on the earth.

He that is righteous stays righteous still, and he that is evil stays evil still. If you are righteous you will always be righteous, and you will gravitate around righteous men and righteous sisters; if you are wicked you will gravitate around wicked people.

The same people who did these things in the past are coming back to do the same thing again. Antiochus died a long time ago under the Greeks, yet it says he shall fight against the prince of princes: the same way he came up against the holy people and killed many of us, he is going to do it again, and when Christ comes back he is going to fight against Christ.

That is why this matters. What was done to us in slavery is a circle coming back around; God’s judgment is as a ring. Slavery is not over. The white man put a smile on his face, and now he is showing you his real face.

precepts.why: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man.” This names the thing of Ecclesiastes 1:9: the thing that hath been, and that shall be again, is man. What man did before, man will do again.

sense.text:
“Therefore saith the Lord, I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness, which they profanely commit.” This is talking about the white man persecuting us and killing us here in America, and the so-called Jewish people afflicting and killing us here in America. Pay attention to what is going on in the world: the things spoken out of this Bible are coming to pass.

“Behold, the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me, and the souls of the just complain continually.” They will kill a lot of innocent black men and Hispanic men here in America.

“And therefore, saith the Lord, I will surely avenge them, and receive unto me all the innocent blood from among them.” God says he is going to take vengeance for the innocent blood of the Israelites that is going to be shed here in America, and he will receive all the innocent blood the white man in America sheds.

“Behold, my people is led as a flock to the slaughter”: that is the slaves, the Israelites, led as a flock to the slaughter.

“I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt.” The land of Egypt here is spiritual Egypt, which is America. Much oppression is going to come on our people here, and you already see things being put in place to bring us under heavy oppression. God is saying he will not let the blacks and Hispanics dwell in Egypt any more, because that is who we are: the children of Israel, God’s people.

“But I will bring them with a mighty hand and a stretched out arm, and smite Egypt with plagues, as before.” The same way he smote Egypt in the past, he will do it again: the same way his people were oppressed in Egypt before, they will be oppressed again, and he will come and deliver them and kill all of their oppressors.

“And will destroy all the land thereof.” This time he is not leaving the land of Egypt standing. The whole land will be destroyed, and that land is this land we are living in today.

“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.” A new kingdom, a new society, that did not respect Joseph or the Israelites. What was done is that which shall be done, and America is spiritual Egypt: the same thing is happening today.

“Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.” Seventy souls went down into Egypt. We went into somebody else’s country as a minority, and over time we became the majority; the Most High made that happen. And before the oppression, it was the children of Israel who had the jobs, who were up in that society and had the businesses set up. Joseph was second in charge.

Mightier means better. We were better than the Egyptians, those Hamites, in trade, farming, education, whatever you can think of, and they knew it.

It is the same here in America. Only about a hundred of us were brought here first, and Esau was the majority after he killed out the North American Indians and took the land. But every couple of years he takes a census. The census is to keep track of you. They call us the new minority groups to trick us, and they divide us up, so many million black people, so many million Hispanics, to make it look like it is not a lot. Don’t let the white man fool you: the twelve tribes of Israel are the majority in America. Their own census shows Hispanic, black and Asian toddlers now outnumber white ones, and that has white men scared to death.

When our people put their minds together, when we are given the same opportunity and education, we excel above every nation on this earth. It has nothing to do with DEI: we are better qualified. That is why they made it against the law for us to read: if we read, we become smarter than them. And that is what it means that the children of Israel are more and mightier.

“Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply.” Dealing wisely is them setting up the institutions of slavery and oppression to keep us at the bottom of their society, so that we do not multiply above them and are not better than them.

How do they stop us multiplying today? Abortions. Planned Parenthood was set up for you, black woman. They put tumors in our sisters through the food they eat; they target you through your DNA, and that is why so many of you sisters suffer with fibroids. That is “let us deal wisely with them.”

For the last sixty years they say they gave us civil rights, a little freedom, integrated us into their society, and in those sixty years we became the majority. That is why the laws are changing now under the Trump administration: snatching people up and deporting them, trying to change the 14th amendment. They are saying, we have to deal wisely with these people, they are becoming more than us. “When there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us.” This is war.

precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” The great city is America. America is spiritual Egypt.

So the same way ancient Egypt set up institutions of oppression and slavery to keep us down in their society, modern-day Egypt, America, has done the same thing. That is why Esau, Edom, the white man, always tries to keep black people at the bottom of society: because when we have the same opportunity, we excel above them.

sense.text: “Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, ye scornful men.” Scornful men are sinful men, men that hate God’s laws. “That rule this people which is in Jerusalem”: the people in Jerusalem are the Israelites, and the scornful men ruling them are the leaders, the leaders of the black community. Sinful men ruled us then, and they rule us today.

“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement.” Back then our forefathers made that covenant with Egypt. In the time of Christ they made an agreement with Rome to stay in power. During the civil rights movement the leaders of that time made a covenant and agreement with the Democrats, with white America, which is hell and death. That is what the civil rights was about.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us”: when judgment comes, they think it will not touch them. “For we have made lies our refuge.” Our people in America have made their refuge in the lies the Democrats sold us in the 1960s. We trust in the lies of Christianity, the lies of their politics, the lies of Santa Claus and Easter. We celebrate Christmas and teach our kids that a white man comes down the chimney with their gift. We trust in lies and do it openly.

“And under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” Some of those civil rights leaders acted like they loved the people when they hated their people and sold them out. Not all of them. Martin Luther King really loved his people, and that is why he was killed. To see who sold him out, look at who benefited most when he died, and who was put up as the new leader of the black community.

What was the agreement? We came to the shores of Virginia as slaves in 1619. When the constitution said all men are created equal, it did not mean us: we were three-fifths of a man, property, like a dog or a horse. We had no freedom of religion and could not take a slave master to court; the men who wrote it owned slaves. Reconstruction said we were free, then Jim Crow made us slaves again legally, the same way ancient Egypt had institutions of oppression. Then came the civil rights movement and the laws of 1964. That is only about sixty-two years ago. People who lynched and raped us then are still alive, in nursing homes, and some are judges and politicians. In 1965 the marchers at Selma were met with violence and told to take their prayers back to their church; that is what the Christian church was set up for. White Christians talk about God so loving the world, but where was that in the 60s, when the plantation owners were all Christians? These Christians are hypocrites, and Christianity is white supremacy; those of our people that follow it are destroyed. It was never only about voting. It was about the right to be treated as a man, as a human, not lynched, not oppressed. A small group of white people had to come together and pass laws to make the rest of their brothers stop lynching, raping and oppressing another human being. This man has no morals, and he does not love you. When those laws were set up they said, don't worry, we will reverse it soon, and that is what they have started doing now.

Ever since the civil rights passed and our leaders made that covenant with America, the white man has put on a mask, a smile, and now he is taking the mask off. Equality was an illusion they told us during the civil rights, an agreement on paperwork: if there were equality, we would be on equal economic standing with everyone else.

Martin Luther King came to see it. His dream of little black boys and girls holding hands with little white boys and girls, he said, had turned into a nightmare. The speech was co-written by Stanley Levison, a Jewish man who also raised the funds for his organization. King said the gains were got at bargain rates and helped the economic side of the nation: integrating the lunch counters, the buses and the parks. We had our own restaurants, our own buses, our own doctors and nurses, and integration sent all our spending power into their corporations. He said many who supported the marches in Selma and Birmingham, the white and Jewish people around him, were not committed to genuine equality for Negroes. When he spoke against the war in Vietnam, he was told it had hurt the budget of his organization: the money coming to him was affected, and remember who his friend was and where that money came from. Five days before he was murdered he said, I’m afraid that we’re integrating into a burning house, a Sodom and Gomorrah. He became a nationalist, speaking of the promised land for us as a people, not America, and that is what got him killed.

The men around him were suspect. Whitney Young of the Big Six advised Kennedy and Nixon about the black community, and his job was to integrate our people into corporate America and give the Negro a stake in the system; to pacify us they gave us jobs. Lyndon B. Johnson and the Democrats bought our votes with those civil rights, knowing black people would vote for them for the next 200 years. They hijacked the civil rights movement, killed its leader and set up puppets after him. And the movement was hijacked: homosexuals, feminists, Jewish people and the Chinese all benefited more from the civil rights than the black Americans who fought and died for it.

precepts.why:
“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him.” The his is the Caucasian race, the white man. God says their soul is not right. You can try to make them right as much as you want, but God says that race of people, their soul is not right. That is why, when the marchers at Selma asked to pray for the white man standing in their way, he would not have it: his soul is not upright in him.

“Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home.” They transgress with wine, they are proud, and they do not stay in their own land. This pinpoints the so-called white man, and not only him but America.

“Who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death, and cannot be satisfied.” Anything he wants, he takes, and the lands he takes it from catch hell. America is never satisfied with what it has. “But gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people.” Which nation on this earth gathers unto it all people? The great melting pot, the United States of America: Chinese, Arabs, and the twelve tribes of Israel too. It is mystery Babylon the great.

So this is a prophecy of America coming into power, and it calls America hell and death. When Isaiah says the leaders made a covenant with death and an agreement with hell, the leaders of our people made a covenant with America.

“Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” The church is the twelve tribes of Israel, the body of Christ. The gates of hell Christ was talking about in that time was Rome, the so-called white man. So hell in that day was Rome.

“If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” If they left Christ alone, all men would believe on him, and they would lose their place with Rome.

That shows the relationship our leaders had with Rome: they had made a covenant and agreement with Rome to stay in power. In the time of Christ, the hell and death was Rome. Today the hell and death our leaders made an agreement with is the United States of America, the United States of Babylon.

sense.text:
The priests “had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise”, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.” They did not want to set by their own culture and the honours of their fathers.

That is what happened to the Negro here in America. Integration is joining a new society while keeping your original culture. The Chinese have their own customs, their own city, their own economic power, buying and selling among each other. The Arabs come here and are still Muslims in their long garments. All nations integrate. But we, the children of the slave trade, were assimilated: we adopted the dominant culture and became indistinguishable from it, losing our own culture. Some of you even put that weave on your head trying to look like a white woman.

You love the white man’s culture, his ways and his god best of all. The Arabs and the Chinese do not worship the white man’s god; China makes it illegal to have a white Jesus church. But our people love their laws and customs better than our own. The holidays we celebrate, the Fourth of July, Christmas and Easter, are European holidays we learned in slavery. The civil rights did not integrate us; it destroyed us. It took away our spending power, our working together and building communities: the money that once went to us now goes to them.

“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore.” God says we will always be oppressed and spoiled evermore.

So when Jim Crow ended and the civil rights started, they implemented another form of oppression: the prisons, war and crime. The civil rights laws, the 13th, 14th and 15th amendments, were written for black people, and they were distorted and turned into political correctness for everybody.

precepts.why:
“Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness.” We despise God’s word and trust in oppression. The oppression is the little trinkets they gave us in the civil rights, which they hijacked and made for everyone: the Chinese, the homos, white women all benefit more than the people who fought and died and shed their blood for it.

To trust in oppression is to follow the god of the people who bought you and enslaved you. You trust in their court system, their religion, their Democrats, their political system. How are you going to worship a god that does not look like you, the god of the man that enslaved and destroyed you? Where was white Jesus when you were in slavery praying to him? It has been sixty years, and there are still ghettos.

“And stay thereon”: and you stay in it. “Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall.”

“For they have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly.” These are the politicians and the civil rights leaders. They healed the hurt our people had been through slightly. They did not fully heal us: they still set up institutions of oppression and began doing things in secret.

“Saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.” The leaders said the white man has changed, he is not lynching us any more, Jim Crow is gone. There is no peace. The institutions were built on racism to destroy our people and keep us at the bottom of society. “Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination?”

“And this was an occasion to deceive the world”: this is how they deceived the Israelites. “For men, serving either calamity or tyranny”: calamity is slavery, something bad that happened to us, and tyranny is the tyrant, the slave master, this oppressive system. We serve in this system. They “did ascribe unto stones and stocks the incommunicable name”: they made idols our God.

“That they erred in the knowledge of God.” The knowledge of God is that we are the children of Israel, that we must keep God’s laws, and that Jesus Christ is a black man. “But whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance”: there is a war going on, and your leaders are telling you it is peace. Ignorance is knowing nothing. Ask our people when Christ was born and they say December 25th; ask who they are and they say, I’m from Africa. The truth is hid from us.

“Those so great plagues called they peace.” The things we live in are plagues, and we call it peace.

sense.text:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships.” That Egypt is America, and the ships are the slave ships. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.”

And it is coming around again. The voting rights are being destroyed and slavery is coming back: commit a crime, and under the 13th amendment you are a slave doing hard time. God is raising oppression back up on our people, and we are going back into the Jim Crow era. There will be civil war here and all kinds of oppression. That is the burning house.

precepts.why:
Chapter 29 is a continuation of 28: it tells what happens to us once we are brought into Egypt on ships. “Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath; But with him that standeth here with us this day before the Lord our God, and also with him that is not here with us this day.”

Him that is not here is us today, in the future: the slaves who would go into Egypt again with ships, brought to America on cargo slave ships.

“And it come to pass, when he heareth the words of this curse”: while you are in America, in the Egypt Moses said you would be in, you hear the words of the curse. “That he bless himself in his heart, saying, I shall have peace.” I follow white Jesus, I’m good, I’m happy. You are living under that illusion.

“The Lord will not spare him, but then the anger of the Lord and his jealousy shall smoke against that man”, the man in Egypt, in America, “and all the curses that are written in this book shall lie upon him.”

“When they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses which the Lord hath laid upon it”: that land is the Egypt the Lord said he would bring us into as slaves. “And that the whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and burning.” That is America. That is Egypt. That is the burning house Martin Luther King said he integrated his people into.

“Like the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah.” His friend said the same thing: King called America a Sodom and Gomorrah, and Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed with brimstone and fire.

sense.text: “Behold, I am against thee, O thou most proud, saith the Lord God of hosts”: the most proud is the white man. “For thy day is come”: your judgment is come, “the time that I will visit thee”, when Christ the Lord visits America.

“And the most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.” All the cities here in America. That is what Martin Luther King saw when he said he had integrated his people into a burning house.

“The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together”: we will be oppressed here in America, and we are together. This shows it is talking about right now. “And all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.” That proves we are still slaves. They never let us go.

“Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is his name: he shall throughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the land, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.” God is going to plead our cause, and the inhabitants of Babylon, America, will be disquieted.
“A sword is upon the Chaldeans, saith the Lord, and upon the inhabitants of Babylon”, which is America, “and upon her princes, and upon her wise men.”
“And upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her”: the mingled people are all the nations living here in America.

precepts.why:
“Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.”

That is the burning. That burnt mountain is the burning house Martin Luther King saw: the fire the Lord kindles in the cities of the most proud.
